title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 88 (Registers of members and security holders)

content.overview: Every company must maintain a register of members (separately by equity/preference class), a register of debenture-holders and a register of other security holders in the prescribed form and manner, with an index of names. A depository's register/index of beneficial owners is deemed the corresponding register/index. If authorised by its articles, a company may maintain a prescribed foreign register for persons residing outside India. Failure to maintain the registers as required attracts a penalty of ₹3,00,000 on the company and ₹50,000 on every officer in default.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 88 (Register of members, etc.). Every company must keep and maintain, in the prescribed form and manner, (a) a register of members indicating separately each class of equity and preference shares held by each member residing in or outside India, (b) a register of debenture-holders, and (c) a register of other security holders. Each register must include an index of names. The register and index of beneficial owners maintained by a depository under section 11 of the Depositories Act, 1996 are deemed the corresponding register and index for the Companies Act. If authorised by its articles, a company may keep a prescribed foreign register outside India containing the names and particulars of members, debenture-holders, other security holders or beneficial owners residing outside India. Under subsection (5), failure to maintain the specified registers or maintain them in accordance with subsections (1) or (2) attracts a penalty of ₹3,00,000 on the company and ₹50,000 on every officer in default. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Required registers
sections.body: Every company must keep and maintain in the prescribed form and manner a register of members showing separately each class of equity and preference shares held by members residing in or outside India, a register of debenture-holders and a register of other security holders.

sections.heading: Index and depository register
sections.body: Every register maintained under subsection (1) must include an index of the names entered in it. The register and index of beneficial owners maintained by a depository under section 11 of the Depositories Act, 1996 are deemed the corresponding register and index for the purposes of the Companies Act.

sections.heading: Foreign register
sections.body: If authorised by its articles, a company may keep outside India, in the prescribed manner, a part of the register called a foreign register containing the names and particulars of members, debenture-holders, other security holders or beneficial owners residing outside India.

sections.heading: Penalty for failure to maintain registers
sections.body: If the company does not maintain the specified registers or fails to maintain them in accordance with subsections (1) or (2), the company is liable to a penalty of ₹3,00,000 and every officer in default is liable to a penalty of ₹50,000.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 88: Register of members, etc.

examples.title: Registers of members
examples.body: Every company must keep a register of members, and registers of debenture holders and other security holders, in the prescribed form.

hypotheticals.question: A company maintains a register of members but does not keep an index of names. Which section 88 requirement is implicated?
hypotheticals.analysis: Subsection (2) requires every register maintained under subsection (1) to include an index of the names included in it. Failure to maintain the registers as required can attract the subsection (5) penalty.

hypotheticals.question: A company wants to maintain a foreign register for members residing outside India. What must it check?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 88(4) permits a foreign register only if authorised by the company's articles and maintained outside India in the prescribed manner for the listed categories of persons residing outside India.

distinctions.title: Section 88 registers and section 90 SBO register
distinctions.left: Section 88 requires registers of members, debenture-holders and other security holders, with an index.
distinctions.right: Section 90 requires the separate significant-beneficial-owner register, returns and identification steps.

rows.left: Record registered membership and security-holder particulars
rows.right: Identify individuals meeting the significant beneficial ownership/control test
Separate current penalty structure under section 90(11)

misconceptions.trap: Treating the section 90 significant beneficial owner register as a substitute for the section 88 registers.
misconceptions.correction: Section 88 specifies the member, debenture-holder and other security-holder registers; section 90 creates separate SBO obligations.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a company may maintain a foreign register without authority in its articles.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (4) expressly conditions the foreign register on authorisation in the articles and compliance with the prescribed manner.

misconceptions.trap: Using the older fine/continuing-fine language for failure to maintain registers.
misconceptions.correction: The current subsection (5) imposes a penalty of ₹3,00,000 on the company and ₹50,000 on every officer in default.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 88 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Every company must keep a register of members, and registers of debenture holders and other security holders, in the prescribed form.

Foreign register requires authority in the articles.
